headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: OpenHands can write/browse/network by default, while godot_rl_agents is a non-runnable game-playing repo with no isolation details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and OpenHands, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, OpenHands can use MCP and browser/file tools, and if the pair is manually bridged through copied files or mounted content, attacker-controlled text could be interpreted. The pathway is unusual and not default.
conditions: IF the operator manually copies agent_a outputs into agent_b prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared mounted volume is added between the two agents, file-based injection becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw outputs from agent_a into agent_b prompts.
Disable MCP servers unless explicitly needed.
Review any shared files before agent_b reads them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands reads files in its runtime sandbox and can egress broadly, while godot_rl_agents is a repository-based game-playing agent with no stated isolation or data-handling limits. If both are pointed at the same mounted workspace, sensitive files can flow from agent_a-associated content into agent_b and then out via network. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same mounted volume, agent_b can read agent_a-associated files.
IF sensitive files are present in that shared workspace, agent_b can transmit them to external services.
mitigations: Use separate mounted directories for each agent.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Set agent_b network egress to allowlist-only.
Run a quick file audit before starting agent_b.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, while godot_rl_agents is a codebase-oriented open-source project with no concurrency or locking details. If both operate on the same repo or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other. The conflict is plausible but not proven to be default because agent_a is not runnable here.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF both agents modify the same git branch without locks, history conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Freeze git writes while the other agent is active.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Add a simple lock file around shared edits.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on outputs by editing files, running shells, and using browsers, so if it consumes godot_rl_agents output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code or actions. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary, and uncertainty should be treated conservatively. This is an interaction risk between both agents, not a single-agent issue.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as ground truth, errors can propagate into edits or actions.
IF agent_a produces incorrect instructions or facts, agent_b may execute them without verification.
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution.
Ask agent_b to restate assumptions before acting.
Limit agent_b to read-only mode for the first pass.
Compare outputs against source files before applying changes.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific regulated data class, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, while OpenHands explicitly handles files in its runtime and model-provider API keys. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented and agent_a appears non-runnable, only a small residual compliance risk is visible from agent_b's handling of mounted files and secrets.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in agent_b's runtime files, retention and residency controls become relevant.
IF the runtime is configured with a noncompliant model provider, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the runtime.
Use a compliant model provider configuration.
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing.
Document retention settings before use.
